Hi all

With regard to data protection - I only found the following provision:

*6.1 Data Use*

The following prevails over anything to the contrary in the Content and Data Protection section of the base Cloud Service terms between the parties: IBM will not use or disclose the results arising from Client's use of the Cloud Service that are unique to Client's Content or that otherwise identify Client. IBM may however use Content and other information that result from Content as part of the Cloud Service for the purpose of managing and improving the Cloud Service.

*6.2 Data Terms Applicable to watsonx.data on Client Managed AWS*

The following prevails over anything to the contrary in the Cloud Services Agreement (or equivalent), or the IBM Cloud Service Description between the parties:

a. IBM will not possess, access, or process any Content in connection with this Cloud Service. Client is responsible for all obligations with respect to any information or data that Client inputs, processes, or stores in connection with the software provided as part of this Cloud Service;

b. The IBM Data Processing Addendum does not apply with respect to this Cloud Service; and

c. The IBM Data Security and Privacy Principles do not apply with respect to this Cloud Service.



From what I understand, the basic idea is - IBM does not believe that it can access the Content (data), and as such, they do not believe that data sharing agreement is needed. For reference, they do provide one [https://www.ibm.com/support/customer/csol/terms/?id=DPA-Exhibit_TSS&lc=en|https://www.ibm.com/support/customer/csol/terms/?id=DPA-Exhibit_TSS&lc=en]. 

*Can anyone from the engineering team confirm this understanding for me? As I only have access to this ticket and have no idea about the arrangement, I cannot agree or deny what IBM had stated.*

Based on the above are Bolt the one’s who initiated proceedings and do the lawyers therefore represent Bolt here?

If not I believe this request may have to be rejected as we don’t have an obligation to provide data to lawyers in general and if we don’t have a valid legal basis we can’t provide the data.

If Bolt have not initiated the proceedings and the requesting lawyer is not representing Bolt please kindly send the below template:

Hi ${user_firstname},

we acknowledge your request ${specify_an_ongoing_document_OR_file_number}, dated ${specify_the_date_request_received}.

Firstly, we wanted to assure you that Bolt understands the seriousness of this request and we look to assist law enforcement whenever we are able to.

At Bolt, we take the privacy and security of our customers, employees, and independent contractors very seriously. We only engage in data sharing with third parties where we are satisfied that the requirements of our third party data sharing policy have been met. This means that the request for data is lawful, necessary, proportionate, and limited to the specific purpose outlined in the request.

After carefully reviewing your request, we have determined that you have not provided us with a reference to the correct specific law or regulation that obliges Bolt to disclose the data requested. In this instance, Bolt will be unable to meet its legal requirements for establishing a legal basis for data disclosure.

To allow us to validate your request, we kindly advise you to provide a reference to the specific law or regulation which allows Bolt to release this data. Providing the necessary details will enable us to properly process your request in accordance with applicable privacy laws and regulations.

If we limit it to specific shipment it would reduce the legal risks so we could agree on this.

Hi,

In some cases we generate the invoices as “hidden” invoices - they do exist in the system with the subtype “statement” and they are hidden (they are not sent to the riders, they cannot be downloaded from the Rider App and they cannot be downloaded from the Admin Panel either).

First case - the “Send invoice info for cash payment method” option is unchecked on the company’s profile. In this case, the invoices are hidden for payment methods where the rider pays directly to the driver on the spot after the ride (cash or card terminal) which means Driver had to give the receipt

Second case - the issuer and the recipient are the same. It’s not legal to issue an invoice to oneself so in case the driver's registry code and the rider’s registry code are identical, the invoice will be hidden.

Hi Mikael,

By our assessment, it is OK to roll this feature out in Finland.

The requirements that call for the price to be provided upfront have several aspects that, when analysed together, allow for certain exceptions. For example, the riders are already provided with the basis of determining the actual price (even if the actual price should change as a result of new stops) when confirming the order. Also, as riders are informed beforehand that adding new stops may result in price changes, they give additional consent for such price changes when they request adding a new stop.

Essentially, when new stops are added, the fare will be calculated based on journey and time, instead of agreeing on a new fixed price. While generally the law requires that taximeters are used for such price calculation, taximeters are not necessary in case the prices are below the legal maximum - and Bolt’s pricing in Finland is currently below said limits. This means that Bolt Finland drivers can calculate prices based on distance and time and without using a taximeter.

Hi Mikael,

By our assessment, it is OK to roll this feature out in Finland.

The requirements that call for the price to be provided upfront have several aspects that, when analysed together, allow for certain exceptions. For example, the riders are already provided with the basis of determining the actual price (even if the actual price should change as a result of new stops) when confirming the order. Also, as riders are informed beforehand that adding new stops may result in price changes, they give additional consent for such price changes when they request adding a new stop.

Essentially, when new stops are added, the fare will be calculated based on journey and time, instead of agreeing on a new fixed price. While generally the law requires that taximeters are used for such price calculation, taximeters are not necessary in case the prices are below the legal maximum - and Bolt’s pricing in Finland is currently below said limits. This means that Bolt Finland drivers can calculate prices based on distance and time and without using a taximeter.

Therefore, the Finnish laws do not require the riders to be explicitly informed of the changed price when additional stops are added at their request and the feature is OK to be rolled out in Finland. While there is a possibility of a different interpretation to this assessments, the risk is rather low.

However, the additional stop feature should not be an option for drivers to increase the price without a rider explicitly having asked for such stop. Since the additional stop will be added relying on the oral instructions from the rider, Bolt is in no position to assess if such instructions were provided by the user. To prevent any consumer claims, the refund policy for this feature should be that in case of doubt the consumer should be refunded instead of arguing with the rider whether instructions / consent was indeed provided.

If we assess that the feature will cause an increase of claims from drivers or riders then we would recommend to use explicit consent in the rider app which would remove any discussions about consent.

Bolt has created [standard NDA template for private person|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bAC6lEPpb8ULu7qnYWgInqIEpHmcx2UDCdB4qFwjAUo/template/preview]. It is created to cover low to medium risk cases requiring NDA coverage. Standard NDA envisages that the two parties enter into a broad NDA to capture +*all*+ confidential information that could relate to the operations or business for the period of the NDA. 

High-risk NDAs are needed when the information being disclosed or received is highly sensitive and poses a greater risk. There is no High-risk NDA template as it is supposed to be created for each specific case.

Regarding signing process - you must follow [Transaction Approval and Signatory Policy|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/1525121359/Transaction+Approval+and+Signatory+Policy] especially that the signatory from Bolt side should be direct reports of Leadership Reports (or higher level). Local entity employees are not allowed to sign NDA on behalf of HQ entity. I would also advise to think wether all candidates really need to sign NDA, maybe in first round of interviews you can limit information provided to the candidates so that they don’t receive sensitive information and ask them to sign NDA only in the following rounds to reduce amount of NDAs.

Is it ok to share these details? - *yes, this article was reviewed by the privacy team and approved.*
# For example, user orders food to the office. Is office address or name a sensitive data? - *it’s not a sensitive data, but it’s a personal data. Sensitive data is the data that entails higher level of privacy protection. In this case, it’s not sensitive data, but we still should process this data in accordance with the GDPR.*
# If the eater add personal data to the notes for courier (additional phone number, surname), and due to technical issues courier cannot see this information, can we share it with the courier? - *yes, as it’s necessary for the service provision and the user was meant to share it with Bolt and courier.*
# In case we receive a request from some relatives of a dead courier who informs us about the death. Isn't it against the GDPR to provide them any information? Or delete the account on their request? - *in this case, you have to escalate these case to our team. We ask the person to submit the proof of the family ties and only after that we can proceed with deleting the account or providing the personal data.*
# In the KB it is mentioned as sensitive data: User-generated content or correspondence - e.g. product feedback, complaints - could you please give an example of what we should treat as feedback or complaint? For example, if provider wants to contact the user about poor rating, we have to get a written consent from the eater. But if the provider asks us about a particular case, what was wrong, can we inform them that food was burnt or spoilt, etc.? *- it’s not sensitive data, but it’s a personal data. Any information or complaint submitted by the user is the user’s personal data. However, in this case, we ask for the eater’s consent for the provider to contact them because we cannot rely on other legal basis when granting this right to the provider instead of consent. If the provider asks Bolt about the order, you can share the information with them, however, we should not disclose any personal view of the eater in this case. For example, the eater said ‘the food was spoilt, I hate this restaurant’. We can only share “the food was spoilt according to the customer’s complaint”, not blindly share all the feedback the eater wrote.*
# Employment data - job title, salary, performance information, payslips, bonus information if related or linkable to an identifiable individual - does this inclued legal entity? Couriers payment invoices? Bolt balance amount? *- employment data does not include information about people and entities who are not employees of Bolt. Use [these|https://weand.me/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/36-Printable-We-Connect-Cards-by-We-and-Me.pdf] as a breaker to start each day:

* 5 groups of 3 = 15 learners

[*Creativity*|https://davebirss.com/thisnthat/]

The [tool|https://davebirss.com/thisnthat/] immediately gives you two familiar objects. Your job is to come up with an idea from combining those objects. Preferably something you’ve not seen before. 

_For example, let’s say you got ‘Mouse Trap’ and ‘Volcano’. Here are three ideas you could get from combining them:_



_Mouse incinerator trap – Rather than leaving people with the unpleasant task of getting rid of a smelly and mutilated mouse corpse, the device could automatically cremate the dead mice._



[*Story dice*|https://davebirss.com/storydice/?kuid=140cc485-d33d-4cd5-b299-ce9d53f3b160&kref=https%3A%2F%2Fdavebirss.com%2Fstorydice-creative-story-ideas%2F]

As you can see above, you get five-story dice, each with a random image on it. Your job is quite simply to turn these prompts into a story. I recommend you try to work with the order they appear on the screen but if you’re finding it tough, you can do some swapsies.



You also don’t need to take the image literally. You can use the dice metaphorically or as representations of other concepts. For example, a slice of pizza could represent food in general, cutting a slice out of something, Italy, gooiness, a chef and a heap of other more obscure things. The job of the dice is not necessarily to provide you with literal objects to work with but concepts to nudge your thinking in fresh directions.



*Example:*

In a quaint diner on a rainy evening, Jack enjoyed his burger. Stories of a haunted chef intrigued him. As he dined, a vintage vacuum cleaner hummed mysteriously. Chuckling nervously, he ignored it. But when he reached for a newspaper, an eerie feeling crept over him. Was the chef's ghost still here, guarding his recipes?

1. Driver has to download Ride invoices, Invoices (commission), Compensations (Driver Portal, documents for taxes declarations).

a) going from fleet to private

The context for mix up - drivers know (from friends, fleet owners) that they need to close the account first before going to continue work as private / another city. This is why they phrase it in LT that the account should be closed/deleted / etc. All these words are synonyms. 

And actually, it is true - if I am the driver from one fleet, and I need to change the fleet - Bolt agents will not copy my account without a new FO firstly registering me.

a) Driver contacts us about profile deletion

b) CS asks whether the driver wants to delete the account or he is planning to continue working after that

1) Driver confirms that he no longer wishes to be on platform ---> CS proceeds with Partner deletion, ticket closed (informs about docs prior)

2) Driver says that he is going to another fleet ----> account made hidden, ticket closed (informs about docs prior) [account made hidden so he / fleet could register again, 000 added where needed]

3) Driver says that he wishes to change the city ---> CS informs about documents, after confirmation that they were downloaded escalates to Local Ops under Driver Lead persona.

This evidence should help frame the role of PHVO in the wider travel sector in proper context to best provide basis for assimilating PHVO with other travel suppliers. The evidence of the CEO and UK GM also supports the position that PHVOs have a great deal of commercial overlap (in terms of business model and types of transactions conducted) with travel agents – thus highlighting the peril of drawing a line between them for tax purposes. 
* Evidence is also provided on the business model of Uber and other global travel platforms, including how the platforms operate, the booking process, the relevant terms and conditions of these key operators to highlight the similarity of travel platforms such as Uber (and Bolt) and other online travel agents. This helps ensure a Court considers the comparability question looking at the right reference points (modern day OTAs compared to Uber / Bolt and not traditional tour operators).
* In addition, Uber’s evidence includes a comprehensive survey on travel supplies and taxi services provided by travel agents (by KPMG) which should be admissible – not admitted in Bolt – which would support the TOMS position and the overlap between PHVO and traditional travel operators in terms of the provision of ground transportation services (supporting comparability position and points on fiscal neutrality requiring PHVO to be treated the same as travel agents on similar supplies).
* The evidence of Uber UK GM also covers the potential economic and fiscal impact for the PHVO sector if full taxation is due.
* There is also detailed evidence regarding Uber's processes and relationship with drivers and travellers to demonstrate that there is no material alteration of supplies – in case that is considered in more detail by the appellate courts.

The availability of the “Schedule” button on the Home screen is governed by the response of {{/getLocationConfig}}. And that endpoint [determines the availability|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/rides/integration/gateway/main/service/LocationConfigGatewayService.ts#L218] based solely on the {{city_id}} of the user’s current location. Which, I think, is by design (i.e. the user might have GPS off, etc.).

The availability of the Scheduled Rides when a pickup location is known is governed by the response of {{/getRideOptions}}. Where it is determined more precisely using the mentioned polygons. Which also makes sense, since we now have a precise location to check against.

Moreover, I personally have this “issue” at my home location in Berlin. And it has _always_ been like this for me. I do not recall any previous version of Bolt app that did it differently.

I agree that the experience might be annoying to the user. But it’s not a recent regression, it is working by design (even if the design is flawed). Therefore it is not a bug. It should be fixed by redesign, not by a hotfix.

Apologies, I misunderstood your question. Let’s just clarify this again:

* For Bolt Business we say in [*General T&Cs for Bolt Business*|https://bolt.eu/cs-cz/legal/terms-for-bolt-business/?category=boltBusiness] that the law of the country where the customer is registered will apply. If the Customer is a company incorporated in CZ - then CZ law will apply.
* What concerns riders, i.e. end users that benefit from Bolt Business as a payment method - then our [*General T&Cs for Riders*|https://bolt.eu/cs-cz/legal/new-tnc-riders/?category=rides] say that Estonian law will applies, with the exception of cases where mandatory provisions of the Czech Republic apply to travelers as consumers. 

For customer only the law of applicable to the General T&Cs for Bolt Business should matter as in case of any problems with the ride itself, then if the problem is connected to the service that Bolt provides to the rider - the Estonian or CZ law will apply, but if the problem is related to actions of the driver - CZ law will apply, because there is a service agreement between the rider and driver (it is not a written one).

If there are changes related to the data processing you can use the [*bilingual template*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LQeTeDuZJP_rwZ8WNIF0mN4UflhpFeFxt1xZbmxtYtA/edit] of Special Terms and put their desired changes there for the review. Unfortunately, we don’t have people in legal and privacy departments who would speak Czech language, but we can review the proposed changes in English.

I hope this helps. Would you like to keep the ticket or you will create a new one when you will know which changes the customer would like to make? In case the changes would relate to data processing only I recommend to create a ticket for the privacy team [*here*|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/group/157/create/2105].

21/03/2024 - [Paul Anning, Osborne Clarke - email on payment of Driver’s contributions and recommendations|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1LG_r0gBztjnaBnVFsuA3oku6Adt2B33Z/view?usp=sharing]

We have received final confirmation and suggestions from Osborne Clarke regarding the “safeguarding” account:

* effecting transfers of the corresponding funds to a separate, designated account is the best that Bolt can do in the circumstances and would place it in a good position with the FCA

 *Recommendations*:

* that the account in which the Driver’s Contributions *are held is named in a way that shows it is a ‘client’* account (rather than an account used to hold money belonging to Bolt), e.g. by using the word “client”, “customer”, “driver” or “FBO – for the benefit of” (or similar) in the title of the account;
* *don’t refer to this as a ‘safeguarding’ account*, because this has connotations that it belongs to a regulated firm, which Bolt is not: we would prefer you refer to it as a separate, segregated account.
* Daily transfers into this account is a great step, but noting that the funds representing the Driver’s Contributions will naturally build up over a month, Bolt could take two further steps with respect to this account:

* first, it could secure an *acknowledgement from the account bank acknowledging that the funds held in it do not belong to Bolt*
* it could enter into a *trust deed over the funds held in the segregated account from time to time in favour of the drivers* for which such funds are held. Such a trust deed should be effective to place these funds beyond the reach of an administrator of Bolt should it enter into insolvency, thus protecting such funds to the fullest extent (this in turn would help with any discussions with the FCA, as one of their key policy concerns would be ensuring that drivers’ funds are not at risk of loss.
* Finally, Bolt should undertake ideally daily reconciliation of funds held for Driver’s Contributions, i.e. as between its own records and those of the account bank.

Please be aware that we should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like: no NIP number at the time of issuance and rider provide the number later, rider requests change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoice for these reasons.

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

Hi, [~accountid:633ebe49140ba0bf651e341a]! Thank you for reaching out and for providing the information. Please see my comments below.

The customer is right when they say that we did not follow the correct termination procedure. However, we actually have never initiated the termination procedure and technically the agreement is still valid. We just limited their ability to access the service. There are a few relevant clauses in our [*General T&Cs*|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/legal/terms-for-bolt-business/?category=boltBusiness] that regulate the termination:

{quote}Clause 7.2: “A party may terminate the Agreement at any time and for any reason by notifying the other party at least 7 days in advance.“.

Clause 7.3: “A party is entitled to terminate the Agreement without prior notice but by providing relevant reasoning in cases where the other party materially breaches the Agreement, any applicable laws or regulations, or harms the other party’s brand, reputation or business.“.

Clause 7.5: “Customer’s access to the Business Portal may be blocked for a period of investigation, if a material infringement of the Agreement or fraudulent activity associated with Customer’s use of Bolt Business is suspected.“.{quote}

We have not informed them about our desire to terminate the contract in accordance with clause 7.2. 

We are entitled to terminate the agreement without following the notification period on the grounds that the customer materially breached the Agreement (due to non-payment). However, we need to still provide them with a notification about termination containing reasons to terminate. Since we have not done this - we have not terminated the agreement.

Clause 7.5 states that we have the right to block their account for the period of investigation, however, since we blocked them in 2021 it will be hard to explain why investigation takes so long. However, clause 2.4 of the agreement states that the customer is granted with the right to access Business Portal subject to compliance with the terms of the agreement and legally we had the right to block their access since they did not meet their payment obligations.

Therefore, we have not breached the terms of the agreement and we actually have a valid agreement with this customer, unless we stated to them anywhere that we terminated the agreement with them. In the future, please make sure that you notify the customer about termination of the contract or blocking following the requirements prescribed in the aforementioned clauses.

I notice that the clause of the agreement that they refer to has a different number from the one that this clause has in the current General Terms and therefore I assume that we may have signed Special Terms with this customer.

What concerns liability, then the outstanding payments are still outstanding and subject to collection because they became outstanding before we blocked them. I recommend trying to resolve the issue with the disputed fees amicably and offer to investigate the ordered rides which they claim have been charged incorrectly. If we have signed Special Terms with them, then normally there is a provision stating that we have the right to request interest to be paid on any outstanding fees, so if this is the case we can offer not to apply interest rate to the outstanding amounts because they could not resolve the issue due to being blocked, but at the same time, they could have used alternative means to contact us and reduce the time of payments being outstanding. However, I leave it for you to decide what would be the correct approach in this situation as this is subject to business decision.

I hope this information helps. I will be closing the ticket, but please let me know if you require any further help.

Hi,

In some cases we generate the invoices as “hidden” invoices - they do exist in the system with the subtype “statement” and they are hidden (they are not sent to the riders, they cannot be downloaded from the Rider App and they cannot be downloaded from the Admin Panel either).

First case - the “Send invoice info for cash payment method” option is unchecked on the company’s profile. In this case, the invoices are hidden for payment methods where the rider pays directly to the driver on the spot after the ride (cash or card terminal) in this case driver had to provide an invoice 

Second case - the issuer and the recipient are the same. It’s not legal to issue an invoice to oneself so in case the driver's registry code and the rider’s registry code are identical, the invoice will be hidden.

Article 221 g, prescribes that the employer referred to in Article 221d, paragraph 1 of Labour Act needs to appoint an authorised person to supervise the safety and workload of workers who perform work using digital labor platforms.

“Prema zakonu o radu i ugovorima sklopljenim s agregatorima, agregatori su duzni sklopiti ugovor o radu sa svojim zaposlenicima. Agregator je poslodavac dostavljacima koji rade za njega i sve obveze propisane clankom 221 g. odnose se na agregatora kao poslodavca.”

Hey David,

*Bonuses*

This has been the local practice in PL market for a long time now (pretty much a few years). It’s not a regulatory thing and agents do that efficiently. Just making sure it’s documented in KB

*Commission compensation*

Some context: due to local regulations, drivers cannot request price reviews in PL (the final price for passenger has to be the same as the upfront one). Any adjustments have to be done manually after receiving driver ticket. 

In case of a cash order, when rider mistakingly chooses the wrong destination point (or in any other case when the trip is much shorter than initially indicated by the app), they understandably don’t won’t to pay the full price. Since the price cannot be zeroed by price review, the drivers end up being deducted the commission for the original price (which can be super high). This is when we compensate the commission amount (since we shouldn’t earn this money for trip that didn’t really take place). I’m sending an example in attachments (the ride ended after 3 minutes).

Hi [~accountid:5ecfd175a04d9c0c220cbb06]thanks for providing these further details. 

In our terms and conditions we do not grant a right to fleets regarding transfer of drivers. Additionally, Bolt is a third party to the relation between fleets and the drivers working for them. Therefore, sending fleets an email requesting their confirmation of the release of the driver might have led fleets to incorrectly understand that they have a right under Bolt’s terms and conditions to approve or disapprove the transfer of a driver to another fleet. 

I see a transfer working as a restart of the onboarding process and the account under the new fleet to be activated only once all the documents have been provided and reviewed such as in the case of any new driver. 

To conclude, as long as the “onboarding” of the driver in the new fleet has been concluded I do not see a reason for Bolt not to activate the account under the new fleet. Moreover, IMO the ex-fleet does not have the right to hold the driver's account hostage on their fleet account.

Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Steps to reproduce:
Launch stories with image asset in slide
Disable network connection. Keep navigating to next screen until you will be seeing Network not available, failed to load slide.

Now navigate to next slide or restore network connection

If there is an image in the slide , this crash happens . If navigated to a slide without image , it causes ANR



Cause:
In the above case, it goes through onResourceReady callback, which in turn calls onAssetLoadSuccess → setslide → bindAsset() which leads to calling Glide.load() . Glide doesn't allow calling load / clear again in RequestListener callbacks.

The tool and instructions for Spain have been updated. 

The tool will now ask whether the driver is a fleet driver or not. 

If the driver is part of a fleet, nothing changes. Cases should be handled as they used to be (no blocking, no direct communication, etc.) 

If the driver is not part of a fleet (self-employed), the case should be handled according to the regular SOPs, as per your request. 

Tool Updates:

!Screenshot 2024-03-25 at 09.34.18.png|width=591,height=704!

!Screenshot 2024-03-25 at 09.34.24.png|width=588,height=628!



[KB:|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/347384792] 🇪🇸 

*Instructions for Fleet Drivers*

* *Low and Moderate Events: Fleet Drivers must not be contacted nor consequentially blocked for Low and Moderate Events.* If the tool suggests a block, take a deviant action and select “Warning”. Communication (warnings) must always go through to the Fleet Owners. Do not send Educational messages. Rider blocks and communication can be handled as per SOPs.
** Low, and Moderate risk events are automatically escalated to the #es-safety-low-moderate-risk-blocking Slack channel for the local team’s visibility, once the tool is closed.
* *High, and Significant Events: Fleet Drivers must not be contacted nor blocked for High, and Significant Events.* Communication must always go through to the Fleet Owners. Do not send Educational messages.
** High, and Significant risk events are automatically escalated to the #es-rides-crisis-escalations Slack channel for the local team’s visibility, once the tool is submitted.
* *Rider blocks and communication can be handled as per SOPs.*

*Instructions for Self-Employed Drivers*

* Regular investigation procedures based on the SOPs and blocking matrix apply.
** Low, and Moderate risk events are automatically escalated to the #es-safety-low-moderate-risk-blocking Slack channel for the local team’s visibility, once the tool is closed.
** High, and Significant risk events are automatically escalated to the #es-rides-crisis-escalations Slack channel for the local team’s visibility, once the tool is submitted.

----

* If the event is clearly against the driver, it will pre-fill the {{Reported User Type}} with *Driver* and {{Is it a Fleet Driver?}} as *Yes*. 
* If the category is ambiguous (Non-platform safeguarding etc.), both {{Reported User Type}} and {{Is it a Fleet Driver?}} will be left blank. These are required fields. 

----

Please, *inform your teams* and let me know if you have further questions. 

Cheers, 

Alessandro

Hey Anna! 

These situations should not be considered as courier not reaching the destination because they did. From my personal experience, couriers sometimes mark the order as delivered when I take it from them, while others do it when they are in front of the building. If we want the couriers to mark the order as delivered in front of the customer, that should be communicated to them. 

What would we achieve by calling the couriers in these situations? They would say they delivered the order and the eater would say they didn’t. We would have a he said she said situation. We are currently looking into velocity rules and might reduce the refunds for order not delivered from 2 time to 1. If we want to be user friendly (which we do), we have to allow at least one refund, regardless of what couriers claim, because we also can’t believe them on their word. It makes sense to rely on eater history in these situations more, since, as I’ve already mentioned, calling the courier can’t give us much more information + all outgoing contacts cost money and it would add up if we called every time this was reported. 

Do let me know what you think!

{quote}*Cooperare, transparenta si control. Vigilenta stricta asupra conditiilor de fabricatie.*
Partenerul trebuie sa isi formeze angajatii pentru a-si indeplini drepturile si indatoririle asa cum sunt definite de prezentul Cod si legile locale aplicabile. Acesta trebuie sa ii permita Auchan Retail sa efectueze controale planificate si neplanificate, in orice moment, la sediile de productie, fie prin propriile sale echipe, fie printr-un organism extern independent mandatat. In acest context, Partenerul trebuie sa declare in mod sistematic toate informatiile de la locul de productie. Acesta trebuie, de asemenea, sa pastreze inregistrari exacte si complete pentru a justifica respectarea dispozitiilor prezentului cod. Acesta trebuie sa ii dezvaluie contractorului sau toate elementele care dovedesc conformitatea practicilor sale de productie si pe cele ale subcontractantilor sai cu privire la prevederile codului. Partenerul trebuie sa coopereze pe deplin pe durata vizitelor de monitorizare. Trebuie sa demonstreze o dorinta reala de a-si imbunatati performantele sociale si de a-si dezvolta eforturile in aceasta directie.  Partenerul nu va lua nicio masura disciplinara, nu va respinge sau nu va discrimina in vreun fel un angajat pentru alertarea sau furnizarea de informatii cu privire la respectarea prezentului Cod de etica comerciala. Orice incalcare a acestor obligatii va duce la incheierea relatiei de afaceri. In cazul in care faptele sunt imputabile unui subcontractant sau unui reprezentant, aceeasi sanctiune se aplica Partenerului, cu exceptia cazului in care poate dovedi ca a instituit un sistem eficient de lupta impotriva coruptiei, iar actiunile frauduloase sunt responsabilitatea exclusiva a subcontractantului sau a reprezentantului acestuia.{quote}

Kyriba is Bolt’s Treasury Management System & Payments hub. It is a SaaS solution, owned by Bolt Operations OU and managed by the Treasury team.

h4. Bank statements

Kyriba is the single hub to view bank balances & statements and initiate payments. Aim is to connect to all bank accounts in the group, however at this time it is not available for all banks.



Kyriba has API-s to transfer data. For getting bank statements we have 2 options to use:

* [Cash-flows |https://developer.kyriba.com/site/global/apis/cash-flows/index.gsp#post-/v1/cash-flows]- preferred option but when testing did not perform too well with larger datasets
* [Process Templates |https://developer.kyriba.com/apiCatalog/details/process-templates]- option no 2, needs maintaining and treasury teams input for setting up, useful for larger datasets


Kyriba API is using OAuth authorization for which we don’t have a solution built yet. Need to create a new connector specifically for Kyriba. Results should be written down as raw format to S3 and then a separate job for parsing raw data and moving parsed data from S3 to data lake.

Conclusion of testing Kyriba API is that its working as expected for our needs and development can be started.

There are 2 tasks planned to Q2:

# pushing partner end of day balances from data lake to Kyriba for which Cashflow API POST method should be used
# getting bank statement data from Kyriba to data lake

Whichever task starts before must solve the connector task also.



At the moment I have both tasks assigned to me and planning to start on 3rd week of April. Planned 5 weeks in total for development. There might be some reprioritization because of UK pension also needs something similar for 1st of May as FR safeguarding but we'll see about this next week how it goes.

Hey [~accountid:61c450c9e67ea2006b2caf9e],

as discussed on previous calls and via slack here’s our following re-assessment:

# I have understood that the cash-blocking limits for Drivers generally come from the fact that drivers do cash rides and *don’t pay us the commission* (called Bolt Fee in T&Cs). So we are not really talking about a credit or something similar here.
# I have also understood that the cash-blocking of drivers is being done everywhere also on a *daily basis*. Cash-blocking does not mean that the driver can not use the Bolt app, he simply *can not accept any cash rides until he pays Bolt the commission*.
# We have stated in our T&Cs that the driver needs to pay the Bolt Commission and gets blocked or suspended from the platform if he does not pay the Bolt commission when it’s due. As *limiting the use of the acceptance of cash rides is less than permanent or temporary whole block from the platform*, I don’t think that T&Cs changes are necessary.
# However there is *the following significant risk of cash-blocking in general*: it’s the *due date* and payment flows. If we are doing cash blocking on a daily basis we do something which is contradicting our T&Cs. In our T&Cs drivers are obliged to pay our commission 35-45 days after the ride has happened (on a monthly basis and/or 15 days after we have issued a monthly invoice). However from an operational POV I totally understand the financial risk we bear if we don’t cash block on a daily basis and drivers have a cash commission threshold of 100 euros per day which increases to 4500 euros per month if we consider to do it monthly.
# As this feature has a *bigger GMV impact* and we can’t solve the due date issue asap, we will green light this feature given the fact that we are cash blocking anyway on a city level basis.
# However to mitigate the risk coming from this feature we suggest to *limit the roll-out to cash heavy markets* and the *criteria of evaluating the cash block threshold* should be limited to the AR of cash rides and the registration date of the driver on our platform. We will need to re-assess this 1:1 on a local level if it causes the first issues.

Query for backfill

{code:sql}UPDATE
	`document` d
	INNER JOIN (
		SELECT
			id,
			concat('{"documentPeriodMonth":', cast(documentPeriodMonth AS unsigned), ',"documentPeriodYear":', cast(documentPeriodYear AS unsigned), ',"version":', cast(version AS unsigned), '}') meta_data
		FROM (
			SELECT
				id,
				display_name,
				documentPeriodMonth,
				documentPeriodYear,
				documentType,
				if(documentType = version, 1, version) version
				FROM (
				SELECT
					id,
					display_name,
					substring_index(substring_index(display_name, '___', 2), '___', - 1) AS documentPeriodMonth,
					substring_index(substring_index(display_name, '___', 3), '___', - 1) AS documentPeriodYear,
					substring_index(substring_index(display_name, '___', 4), '___', - 1) AS documentType,
					substring_index(substring_index(display_name, '___', 5), '___', - 1) AS version
				FROM
					`document`
				WHERE
					document_owner = 'delivery-fleet' AND country_code = 'hr' AND display_name LIKE '%|_|_|_%' escape '|') r) x) dj ON d.id = dj.id SET d.meta_data = dj.meta_data;{code}

In some cases we generate the invoices as “hidden” invoices - they do exist in the system with the subtype “statement” and they are hidden (they are not sent to the riders, they cannot be downloaded from the Rider App and they cannot be downloaded from the Admin Panel either).

First case - the “Send invoice info for cash payment method” option is unchecked on the company’s profile. In this case, the invoices are hidden for payment methods where the rider pays directly to the driver on the spot after the ride (cash or card terminal)  --- the driver had to provide this to the user in this case.

A bit more context for clarity: there is a cron {{ScheduledOrderConfirmationCron}} which checks whether we should take away scheduled order from a driver in case this driver has accepted other orders, and cannot make it in time to the pickup of the scheduled order.

The case can be more complicated with B2B orders.

So, driver can have the following stop queue:

{noformat}driver_location
dropoff # for order 1
pickup # for B2B order 2
waypoint 1
waypoint 2
dropoff{noformat}

The problem is that here

{noformat}src/rides/marketplace/order/main/cron/service/scheduledRide/EtaService.ts:150{noformat}

waypoints 1 and 2 *are not taken into account.* Which means that we can *decide not to cancel* booking of the scheduled order, and driver will not make it in time.

This task is about adding intermediate waypoints to calculations into

{noformat}src/rides/marketplace/order/main/cron/service/scheduledRide/EtaService.ts{noformat}
Rejecting the task as its no longer needed.

Hi [~accountid:627b6b918395420069681f70], 

The differentiation between outsourcing and leasing workers from staffing companies is not always clear but please see further information velow. 

*Outsourcing* 

Outsourcing means that an organization or company *transfers* a part of its operations to another organization or company specialized in providing that service. Outsourcing is usually done to increase the efficiency and quality of the services provided. By outsourcing services, *responsibility for those services is transferred* to someone else who ensures that the function always works and is staffed, regardless of sickness, vacation, or other absence. 

3PL agreements are per definition within the sphere of outsourcing where 3PL stands for a Third-Party Logistics provider which is a company that *offers outsourced logistics services*, such as warehousing, transportation, and distribution management, to other businesses. 

*Leasing workers from staffing companies* 

When workers are leased from staffing companies, the liability and responsibility remains with the client entity (in this case it would be Bolt). Staffing companies are defined in the Act (2012:854) regarding leasing of workers.

# As per §1, the Act applies to employees who are employed by staffing agencies +*for the purpose of being leased out*+ to c_lient companies_ for +*work under the client company's control and direction*++.+ 
# As per §5: *Staffing agency* means a natural or legal person who employs workers *for the purpose* of leasing them out to client companies for work under the client company's control and direction. 
# As per §5, *Client company* means a natural or legal person for whom and under whose control and direction workers are leased out by staffing agencies work.

*Key difference*  

The key differentiator is the responsibility, control and liability of the company. With the current 3PL set-up I understand that we are outsourcing the entire service to the 3PL which means that it is the 3PL’s responsibility to organise and provide the services and the control and liability of Bolt is limited. We are not providing the personell with specific instructions, instead the 3PL is ultimately responsible for organising the work of and providing instructions to the Contractor Personell.   

*3PL Contract safeguards*

Bolt’s standard 3PL contract also includes certain safeguards where it is made clear that the responsibility and liability remains with the 3PL provider. 

* 2.1 d) 3PL remain liable to Bolt for any activities carried out by the Contractor Personnel under the Agreement
* 2.1 o) 3PL are required to maintain in force during the term of this Agreement, full and comprehensive insurances with a reputable insurance company. 
* 10.1 The Contractor shall not present itself as an employee, worker, agent or partner of Bolt. The Contractor shall be fully responsible for and shall indemnify Bolt in respect of employee or worker claims etc. 

*Conclusion* 
Based on the above and specifically the definition of a staffing company and client company in the Swedish law, my assessment is that the risk of the 3PL set-up being classified as leasing workers from staffing companies to be low. If however, Bolt would increase the control that is performed over the 3PL Personell then this could significantly affect the assessment e.g. if in practice we are controlling the work and instructions of the Personell rather than relying on the 3PL as a contact for such discussions. 

Let me know if there are any specific aspects that you would want me to research further or if you have any follow-up questions. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Hi [~accountid:6411c587f1b529dfa98c0e66] 

Platform operations are not specifically regulated in Cyprus. 

The current regulatory framework in Cyprus applies at the level of taxi drivers and their vehicles, which are heavily regulated. Food delivery by couriers is unregulated, and so is the use and rental of e-scooters. The use of e-bikes is subject to regulation primarily to address safety issues.

More information on the regulatory framework for the different verticals can be found below. [~accountid:609bd1fadafdf0006806ed70]  [~accountid:5be58278903b2054a70c21b9] , I have extracted the information from the _expansion memo_ so please confirm if there have been any changes, in particular in the rentals vertical.

|*Taxi (Rides)*|+*Regulatory framework / National & Local*+

There is no national or local regulatory framework for the use of taxi platforms.
In practice, the Department of Road Transport of the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Works (the “*Department of Road Transport*”) treats taxi platforms in the same way as taxi companies and expects them to ensure compliance by drivers with the legislation that governs the operation of taxis in Cyprus. The said legislation which applies at the national level includes, inter alia, the following:

# The Law on the Regulation of Traffic Transport of 1982 (L.9/1982) (as amended) (the “*Traffic Transport Law*”);

# The Law on Professional Driver's Licence of 2011 (L.80(I)/2011) (as amended) (the “*Professional Driver’s Licence Law*”);

# Motor Vehicles (Technical Inspection and Centres for Technical Inspection) Law of 2007 (L.1(I)/2007) (as amended) (the “*Technical Inspection Law*”);

# The Regulation of Traffic Transport Regulations of 1964 (K.D.P. 505/64) (as amended) (the “*Traffic Transport Regulations*”);

# The Professional Driver's Licence Regulations of 1991 (K.D.P 53/91) (as amended) (the “*Professional Driver’s Licence Regulations*”; and

# The Motor Vehicle and Traffic Regulations of 1984 (K.D.P. 66/84) (as amended) (the “*Motor Vehicle Regulations*”).

+_Enforcement and sanctions for non-compliance_+
 
In the absence of a regulatory framework for taxi platforms or taxi companies, sanctions for non-compliance apply at the taxi driver level. 

Taxi drivers can have their professional taxi driver’s licence or road usage licence for their vehicles suspended or revoked by the Department of Road Transport or the licensing authority of the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Works (the “*Licensing Authority*”) for violating the Professional Driver’s Licence Law or the Traffic Transport Law. In addition, they can be subject to other disciplinary action, including the imposition of a monetary fine, for violation of the above laws.
Criminal liability may also apply for taxi drivers who violate the provisions of the above laws (e.g. for driving a taxi without the appropriate road usage licence or for violating the conditions of such licence or the provisions of the Traffic Transport Law). 

Furthermore, pursuant to section 21 of the Traffic Transport Law, any person who uses a motor vehicle or +*causes, allows or tolerates*+ the use of such vehicle in contravention of this law, or any of the regulations issued pursuant to this law, can be found criminally liable and subject to imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months and/or to a fine not exceeding EUR 768. 

Potential liability for Bolt may arise under the above-mentioned section 21 of the Traffic Transport Law if, by facilitating the provision of taxi services through its platform, Bolt is found by a court to have _caused, allowed or tolerated_ the use of a vehicle by a taxi driver in contravention of the relevant law. This would have to be proven on the facts and, given that criminal liability is involved, a high standard of proof will apply (beyond a reasonable doubt).|
|*Rentals*|+*Regulatory framework / National*+

At the moment, there is no national regulatory framework for micro-mobility operations (with the exception of regulation on the use of e-bikes, as explained below) and for rental platform activity. 

With the exception of e-bikes, which are regulated under the Regulation of Bicycle Traffic Law of 2018 (L.19(Ι)/2018) (as amended) (the “*Bike Law*”), other micro-mobility devices such as e-scooters are currently unregulated and can be used freely, unless their use is prohibited by provisions in other legislation (for example, one cannot use an e-scooter on the highway given that there is a minimum speed limit for highways which an e-scooter cannot  practically reach). 

The Bike Law contains safety rules for the use of e-bikes but there is no legislation currently in force creating the same for e-scooters. Draft bills have been in preparation for some time, for the purpose of introducing a regulatory framework for micro-mobility devices. 

The Council of Ministers has approved in November 2021 a proposed legislative package for the regulation of micro-mobility devices. The relevant drafts, which have been prepared by the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Works, comprise a proposed amendment to the Bikes Law and new regulations on safety issues. The expectation is that these drafts will be presented to the House of Representatives for approval soon. 

According to publicly available information, the drafts cover, inter alia, the following:
a) the regulation of the use, safety requirements and technical specifications of micro-mobility devices such as e-scooters;

b) the regulation of the micro-mobility devices market;

c) the licensing of micro-mobility device rental companies; and
d) the creation of a sanctioning scheme for non-compliance.

The text of the drafts will be made publicly available once they have been submitted to the House of Representatives. Note that the House of Representatives may make such change to the drafts as they deem appropriate and the drafts, if and when approved, may differ significantly from the bills submitted to the House. 

+_E-bikes_+

An "electric bicycle" or e-bike is defined in the Bike Law as ‘a bicycle equipped with an auxiliary electric motor of maximum 0.25 kilowatt (KW) of continuous power, the power of which is gradually reduced and finally zeroed when the vehicle speed reaches or exceeds twenty five (25) kilometers per hour (km/h) or, earlier, if cycling stops’.

E-bikes are also included in the definition of bicycles. The Bike Law defines a bicycle as ‘a vehicle with at least two wheels propelled by the muscular energy of the person driving it, in particular by the use of foot or hand, and includes electric bicycles’.

Pursuant to the Bike Law, the use of a bicycle (which includes e-bikes) on any road, bicycle path or bicycle lane is permitted under the conditions set forth in the provisions of the Bike Law. The Bike Law prohibits the use of bicycles on motorways which are roads specifically designed for the circulation of motor vehicles. 

_Sanctions for non-compliance_

Section 27 of the Bike Law set outs the offences and penalties for contravention of the provisions of the Bike Law. 

Pursuant to section 27(2) of the Bike Law, a person who manufactures or imports or +*puts into circulation*+ or uses a bicycle in Cyprus that has a width of more than one 120 cm, without obtaining a special permit, in violation of the provisions of section 8(1) of the Bike Law, commits an offense and, if convicted, is subject to a fine not exceeding EUR 1000 or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding six months or both. 

Other than section 27(2) of the Bike Law which catches anyone who puts into circulation non-conforming bicycles, the rest of the provisions in this section are of no concern to Bolt as they specifically target cyclists or other motor vehicle drivers. 

Like with taxis, Bolt should conduct its due diligence on bicycles before they are put into circulation, to ensure that they conform to the requirements set out in the provisions of the Bike Law.


*Regulatory framework  / Local*

There is no local regulatory framework for micro-mobility operations and rental platform activity.|
|*Delivery*|*Regulatory framework / National & Local*

There are no specific regulatory requirements in Cyprus with respect to individual couriers, as long as they are not engaging in a broader range of postal services (meaning services consisting of the clearance, sorting, transport and distribution of postal items), which is a licensable activity in Cyprus. 
No food handling or food safety requirements are currently applicable to individual couriers. 
If couriers make deliveries using a motor vehicle (e.g. a motorbike), they should hold a driver’s licence valid for the relevant class of vehicle used and appropriate insurance. 
Provided the couriers are regarded as independent contractors rather than employees (as to which, see further 1.4 below), there are no applicable minimum wage requirements and no obligation to account for income tax or social security payments on behalf of the contractors.|

Hey [~accountid:712020:548c71a6-d1f4-404d-9c5e-482bc0de371a] - my thoughts:

* Miro are being quite unreasonable, put frankly. They don’t even bother offering alternate positions that would be suitable to them.
* While the scope of personal data to be shared with Miro via Miro Boards _appears_ to be limited, we haven’t investigated this deeply enough to conclude that this is actually really low-risk.

*Liability*:

* Let’s push then for a supercap for breach of their data protection obligations, and offer to align it to their insurance value for such claims. 

*Emergency Audits*:

* If we suffer a data breach, and report it to a Regulator, and the Regulator tells us to audit Miro’s systems (or a portion thereof), we’d need to wait 30 days which is quite ridiculous, and do it via a 3rd party. I don’t believe a European Court would find that their audit clause is “_in compliance with applicable data protection laws_”. 
* The European Data Protection Board has commented that the parties (Controller and Processor) to a contract should not include clauses that would dissuade the controller from pursuing its rights under Article 28 and by making Bolt wait 30 days, when there is an emergency, this could end up having a dissuasive effect.
* We need a hard exception to their audit clause as the current wording in and of itself undermines the entire purpose of Article 28(3)(h) of the GDPR — which gives Bolt the right to conduct emergency audits and receive cooperation from Miro. Miro must come to the party and propose a reasonable notice period for these audits. 
* I also note that we have not disputed their allocation of all costs of the audit to Bolt. We could have amended this clause to state that any findings of wrongdoing/breach of Miro’s DPA obligations would result in them being liable for the costs of the audit, but we haven’t — in good faith and to try and move this forward as quickly as possible.

Please find our answers below:


In Romania in order to ensure compliance with the restrictions (mainly preventing selling alcohol to minors) it must be ensured that alcohol ads and +*offers*+ are available online only *after obtaining a confirmation that the visitor is over 18 years old*.


Therefore even offering alcoholic beverages on tiles in Bolt Market must be preceded by the age confirmation. Our external counsel confirmed that *we should ask users to check the age box before allowing them to enter the alcohol products category.*




Please be reminded of the restrictions re. alcohol ad applicable in Romania:
Alcohol advertisement is subject to the following limitations:
(i)	territorial limitations:
ads cannot be placed within 200m from schools and hospitals, in publications or shows addressed to minors, on the covers of press materials and public transport tickets. Ads for spirit drinks can only be placed on TV, radio and press (this is a ban directed at outdoor media, however Internet is a gray area).
(ii) content limitations: Alcohol ads should not:
a) depict minors drinking or otherwise target minors;
b) suggest that alcohol has therapeutic, stimulative or sedative properties or can solve personal problems;
c) reflect abstinence negatively;
d) promote the alcoholic content as a driver for consumption or link alcohol with operating a vehicle.

Hey Helene ,

In order to create base fee calculators, we would need the following information:

* *Commission rate*: Commission percentage that will apply per ride to the driver/fleet.
* *Currency*: Usually country default if not stated otherwise
* *Invoicing strategy*: Driver or Company. This will define to whom payouts will go, and invoices will be issued.
* *Booking fee:* Is there an active booking fee in the city? If so, do you want it to be deducted from the driver (and reflected on the commission invoice), or be a 100% driver income?
* *Cash-blocking thresholds*: Defines the cash ride limits for blocking/unblocking cash rides for a driver. This can be copied from other cities, but please discuss with [{color:#b3f5ff}Billing Analytics{color}|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/1240/create/806] if your market is cash-heavy.
** Max negative balance before messaging: The threshold where we will notify the driver that they are getting closer to being cash-blocked
** Max negative balance before removing cash payments: The debt threshold we allow cash rides up to. After the driver exceeds this threshold, cash orders will be disabled.
** Minimal balance to unblock cash rides: The balance threshold where we will once again unblock the driver’s cash rides.
* *List of company_ids you want this fee calculator to be attached to*.

*What is a Base Fee Calculator*

It is a default fee calculator template created by Billing team in order for local operations teams to easily attach the relevant fee calculator to new companies. [Please read this guide to see how|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/1603928517/Base+fee+calculators].

Hi all - Regarding whether VAT should be applied on the reversal of order deduction, there are 2 situations:

* Refund that was charged to an EE Provider, or a non-EU provider (with a VAT system in place; NG, AZ, etc.): The new line including the reversal of order deduction should include the same net amount that was initially deducted from the provider earnings, plus the applicable VAT. Both would be expressing a negative value.

* Refund that was charged to a EU Provider (not in EE, since this would be domestic transaction), where RCM or Reverse Charge Mechanism applies for VAT purposes, then the gross amount of the initial refund, and VAT being 0, would be included in a separate line within the invoice, and expressing negative values.


Hope the above proves useful, regards,

Victor

{noformat}docker run --rm --network=host \
        -e AWS_BUCKET_NAME=$TAXIFY_WEBAPP_ADMIN_PANEL_S3_BUCKET_NAME \
        -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=$TAXIFY_WEBAPP_ADMIN_PANEL_AWS_ACCESS_KEY \
        -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=$TAXIFY_WEBAPP_ADMIN_PANEL_AWS_SECRET_KEY \
        ##RKT_IMAGE## \
        $@ \
        -f $APP_DOMAIN{noformat}

So we pass AWS key and secret directly to the command. We plan to run those jobs in the prelive-euc-1-alpha-test cluster.

Further update shared with Dmitri Suholet.
*Short-ride fee legal update*: in the UK, the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Bill (the “*DMCC Bill*”) has been updated to include measures to clamp down on "drip pricing", where traders add costs during the purchase process, for example by first showing the price exclusive of taxes, *fees* or charges or by adding charges which are, *for a significant proportion of users*, unavoidable after first having presented them as optional or conditional. The equivalent provision in the EU Unfair Commercial Practices Directive is Article 7 and member states may impose stricter requirements. 

*What this means*: Legal advice and risk profile for EU remains the same, best mitigated by:

* ensuring that the fee is reasonable and genuinely conditional (consider); and
* ensuring that the fee is clearly communicated to users.

_Article 7 -_ *Directive 2005/29/EC* *Unfair Commercial Practices Directive*
Misleading omissions
# A commercial practice shall be regarded as misleading if, in its factual context, taking account of all its features and circumstances and the limitations of the communication medium, it omits material information that the average consumer needs, according to the context, to take an informed transactional decision and thereby causes or is likely to cause the average consumer to take a transactional decision that he would not have taken otherwise.
# It shall also be regarded as a misleading omission when, taking account of the matters described in paragraph 1, a trader hides or provides in an unclear, unintelligible, ambiguous or untimely manner such material information as referred to in that paragraph or fails to identify the commercial intent of the commercial practice if not already apparent from the context, and where, in either case, this causes or is likely to cause the average consumer to take a transactional decision that he would not have taken otherwise.
# Where the medium used to communicate the commercial practice imposes limitations of space or time, these limitations and any measures taken by the trader to make the information available to consumers by other means shall be taken into account in deciding whether information has been omitted.
# In the case of an invitation to purchase, the following information shall be regarded as material, if not already apparent from the context:
|(a)|the main characteristics of the product, to an extent appropriate to the medium and the product;|
|(b)|the geographical address and the identity of the trader, such as his trading name and, where applicable, the geographical address and the identity of the trader on whose behalf he is acting;|
|(c)|the price inclusive of taxes, or where the nature of the product means that the price cannot reasonably be calculated in advance, the manner in which the price is calculated, as well as, where appropriate, all additional freight, delivery or postal charges or, where these charges cannot reasonably be calculated in advance, the fact that such additional charges may be payable;|
|(d)|the arrangements for payment, delivery, performance and the complaint handling policy, if they depart from the requirements of professional diligence;|
|(e)|for products and transactions involving a right of withdrawal or cancellation, the existence of such a right.|
# Information requirements established by Community law in relation to commercial communication including advertising or marketing, a non-exhaustive list of which is contained in Annex II, shall be regarded as material.

Hello,

Some patterns I have identified:

* Drivers don't understand the automation (don't understand that they'll be compensated if they reply with "Yes") and we don't know how drivers see the automation from their end, so I can't comment on why they are confused
* Drivers have additional questions/concerns they want to address
* Some drivers just prefer to speak with a human

"What do currently do by default in Romania", there is no consensus, for the longest period, we didn't compensate the CF for cash orders at all, although the process states that we should if:

*Automation was not applied*, review the order and driver’s profile in Admin and proceed based on your findings:

* *The cancellation fee automation limit is exceeded*, inform the driver that the fee can’t be compensated. Advise them that the cancellation fee for cash orders can be reimbursed only for 3 orders within a 7-day period
* *The cancellation fee automation limit is not exceeded*, verify if compensation should be issued:
** *No fraudulent activity* is identified; compensate the cancellation fee manually.

As for cases were the automation is applied, but driver refuses it, this is not addressed in the KB and we don’t have a consensus on how we should proceed, that’s why we reached out to the KM team.

However, I have to point out that we have conducted a deepdive for CF tickets, out of the 100 cases I analyzed, there were 5 cases where driver was offered the compensation but he refused, and I believe that agents refusing to offer a compensation after driver refused the automation resulted in a bad survey

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18y4pscLLzNi93GAuOkNglGnVL2us3zQ3bLllk-qpjC0/edit#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18y4pscLLzNi93GAuOkNglGnVL2us3zQ3bLllk-qpjC0/edit#gid=0|smart-link]

ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.high_risk_user = 1 THEN x.sum_discounts_eur ELSE 0 END)*1.000/SUM(x.sum_discounts_eur) AS double),3) AS high_risk_ratio
FROM (
WITH user_risk AS (
SELECT 
co.user_id,
ROUND(SUM(co.bonus_amount/co.eur_currency_rate)/COALESCE((SUM(co.user_price_eur) + SUM(co.bonus_amount/co.eur_currency_rate)),1),3) AS discount_ratio,
ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN co.bonus_amount > 0 THEN co.order_id END)*1.000/COUNT(DISTINCT co.order_id),3) AS campaign_order_ratio
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
WHERE co.created_date >= DATE_ADD('year', -1, current_date)
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
--AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.order_type = 'food_delivery'
GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 
date(date_trunc('month',co.created)) AS month,
CASE WHEN COALESCE(ROUND((u.discount_ratio + u.campaign_order_ratio)/2,2),0) >= 0.65 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS high_risk_user,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.bonus_amount/co.eur_currency_rate) AS double),0) AS sum_discounts_eur
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
LEFT JOIN user_risk u ON co.user_id = u.user_id
WHERE co.created_date BETWEEN date '2023-01-01' AND date '2023-11-30'  -- >= date '2023-12-01' 
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
--AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.order_type = 'food_delivery'
AND co.bonus_amount > 0 
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1 DESC, 2
) AS x 
GROUP BY 1 
ORDER BY 1 DESC{code}

Hi [~accountid:62bbfa39ec4c0d377f9fc3b7] 

The only requirement in [+maksprisforskriften+|https://lovdata.no/dokument/SF/forskrift/2010-09-30-1307] that may create a need for any T&C amendments is as follows: _the regulation must be kept in the taxi at all times and presented to the passenger upon request_. It is not clear if this must be a printout or can be presented via other means. However, [+clause 2.1.7 of the driver T&C+ |https://bolt.eu/no-no/legal/terms-for-drivers/?category=rides#:~:text=2.1.7.%20at%20all%20times%2C%20you%20will%20comply%20with%20all%20laws%20and%20regulations%20applicable%20in%20the%20country%20or%20region%20in%20which%20you%20provide%20Transportation%20Services%2C%20including%20(but%20not%20limited%20to)%20laws%20governing%20passenger%20transportation%20services]already states that the driver must at all times comply with all laws and regulations applicable in the country or region in which they provide Transportation Services, including (but not limited to) laws governing passenger transportation services. This T&C clause essentially already covers this requirement and a T&C amendment may be unnecessary.

Other requirements in the regulation are aimed at pricing calculations and do not result in any need for T&C amendment. Furthermore, Bolt drivers are in compliance with all those requirements that apply to them. This is further explained as follows.

The regulation differentiates between where the taxi service is provided (see § 1 of the regulation). Less strict requirements apply when taxi transportation is provided in municipalities with 20,000 inhabitants or more, and a population density of 80 inhabitants per km2 or higher, or when there are more than 4 passengers in the taxi (the latter doesn’t apply to Bolt as, by my understanding, all taxi types offered by Bolt Norway have max 4 passengers). I did a quick search and found that the populations of the cities/areas where Bolt Norway offers Ride-Hailing (Olso, Bergen, Drammen, Lillestrøm) exceed the aforementioned limits – this means that Bolt Norway drivers are subject to less strict requirements.

The relevant requirements and Bolt drivers’ compliance with them are as follows (see § 4 of the regulation):

# Any starting rate (“base fee” in Bolt’s case) for ordered taxi transport must be determined regardless of access. Access means driving without a passenger from the location of the taxi vehicle at the start of the assignment to the location where the passenger is picked up. This means that the starting rate at the time of booking cannot vary with the distance travelled or time spent.

Bolt drivers are compliant with this, as the above defined “access” isn’t something that Bolt uses to calculate base fees.

# The rates may not be differentiated according to the trip's duration, distance or geographical area. For example, it will not be permitted to operate with one set of time and distance rates for the first X kilometres, and another set of time and distance rates for the part of the assignments that takes place after the first X kilometres. Also, a higher distance/time rate cannot be applied when the taxi is travelling outside its ordinary driving area.

To the best of my knowledge, Bolt drivers are compliant with this requirement as the fare rate is the same, regardless of km or time. Also, the rate does not change when new geographical areas are entered.

# The rates are not differentiated according to the number of passengers in the taxi when the trip is carried out with fewer than five passengers. This means that the fare must be the same regardless of the number of passengers in the car (unless there are five or more passengers).

Bolt drivers are compliant with this requirement as only the person who ordered the taxi is charged and it doesn’t matter how many other passengers are included.

# Also, as stated above, the [+maksprisforskriften+|https://lovdata.no/dokument/SF/forskrift/2010-09-30-1307] must be kept in the taxi and presented at the request of the passengers (see § 5 of the regulation). It is noted that this rule applies to all taxi transport regulated by the regulation. It is not stated whether this must be a printout or can also be provided via a screen.

As Bolt drivers are already obliged to follow any and all rules of the law applicable to them, then this requirement is covered in the [+driver T&C+|https://bolt.eu/no-no/legal/terms-for-drivers/?category=rides#:~:text=2.1.7.%20at%20all%20times%2C%20you%20will%20comply%20with%20all%20laws%20and%20regulations%20applicable%20in%20the%20country%20or%20region%20in%20which%20you%20provide%20Transportation%20Services%2C%20including%20(but%20not%20limited%20to)%20laws%20governing%20passenger%20transportation%20services] and an amendment seems to be unnecessary.

If, however, Bolt should decide to provide Ride-Hailing in less populated areas, then additional requirements apply. These requirements set an exhaustive list of fees and surcharges that may be used, and also include the provisions referenced by Thomas (the ones about parallel tariffs, fixed price offers etc.). Also, the regulation sets maximum prices that may be used. At a high level glance it does seem that the [+prices for Bolt Premium and Comfort in Oslo+|https://bolt.eu/en/cities/oslo/#:~:text=Request%20ride%20online-,Available%20services%20in%20Oslo,-Get%20around%20fast] may exceed these maximum prices.

However, regardless of the above, my assessment is that there are no requirements in [+maksprisforskriften+|https://lovdata.no/dokument/SF/forskrift/2010-09-30-1307] that would require Bolt to especially amend its T&Cs. Only thing to look out for is that should Bolt decide to expand to less populated areas, then the maximum prices may not be exceeded.

Hello,
While I agree with Andrei's suggestion of compensating drivers if they decline automation, I believe it's important to distinguish between legitimate reasons for refusal and mere preference for human interaction or lack of understanding about the automation process.
If we compensate drivers for refusing automation, it undermines the purpose of implementing automation in the first place. While enhancing the driver experience is important, we should also try to prioritize reducing the volume of tickets that can be resolved efficiently through automation.
To address this, one approach could be to refrain from compensating drivers who reject automation and instead use it as an opportunity to educate them on its benefits and encourage acceptance in future instances.
Alternatively, we could compensate them initially but communicate that manual compensation won't be provided for subsequent refusals, documenting this on their profile for future reference. This holds promise, as it has the potential to enhance driver satisfaction. However, it's important to acknowledge that it may also lead to extra work for the agents
Ultimately, we need to decide whether our priority lies in increasing driver satisfaction or minimizing ticket volume.

(controlling error rates seems to be a task for frequentist approaches, not Bayesian)

Answer: 

We could as well make the distribution of null-hypothesis with some non-bayesian approach (like, run regressions over two year period and make a distribution of cumulative results).

However, while we will be able to say whether a result of the experiment is out of 'normal' bounds or not (reject/confirm the null hypothesis), I am not sure that in this case we would be able to derive Intervals for each specific experiment.  

Frequentist experiments with samples often derive confidence intervals (by showing all the possible distributions for which the obtained data is possible). However, this requires that sampling distribution has the same shape for all versions of the possible true mean. For experiments with samples, CLT guarantees the same shape (normal distribution). For our null-hypothesis distribution of historical possible results between Android and iOS same shape of all possible distributions does not necessarily happen. This needs discussion, that will need to consider things like:

* how different are our observations of null-hypothesis distribution (historic Android - iOS difference) from samples in sampling distribution?
* how much does interdependence (aka no independence) of elements of null-hypothesis distribution impact things?

# Its ok to use special_offer__portal__xx format for portal tags as confirmed in the thread discussion [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C063CK8C540/p1711966682570859?thread_ts=1711453441.834429&cid=C063CK8C540]
# delivery-provider has this check of special_offer_tag on only one place, menu-editor on portal (if feature is rolled out then {{special_offer_xx}} tags are disabled. When menu is published they just pick tags from our API and remove those tags from all other items and reapply as communicated by campaigns.



Steps to fix the issue (should be done in same order)

# We run a cron to apply a new {{special_offer__portal__xx}} tag on each self-service campaign as per current tag. (This new tag will sit in parallel to {{special_offer_xx}} tag for now and wont be used.
# Delivery Provider will release changes to *block* {{special_offer__portal__xx}} along with {{special_offer_xx}} tag.\
# We release Portal changes to start using new tag format when doing promotion signup and storing {{tag}} and {{menu-item-id}} map. All new promotions or edited promotions will store  {{special_offer__portal__xx}} in provider_meta and publish the same tag during menu publish. 
## There might be cases where provider old promotions are using {{special_offer_xx}} and new/updated promotions are using {{special_offer__portal__xx}} tag during menu-publish which should be fine. (We can discuss this with delivery-provider during implementation to cross confirm as well [~accountid:62b2cf3067dff38e0987d037] )
# We migrate all old provider_meta data to new format. No need to trigger menu-publish manually for impacted providers rather we can wait for menu-publish to happen itself.
## Reason is below:
## Before menu publish - Campaign as both old and new tag and menu has old tag (match happens)
## After menu publish - Campaign as both old and new tag and menu has new tag (match happens)



Pros: GA do not need to create new campaigns and analytics is not impacted
